issues.description: Method mismatch: The exercise (UML and textual instructions) defines Animal.messageOnFeed() as an abstract method that returns a String (the song and tasks expect plain String messages like "Arf Arf!", "Oink!", "Maah!"). In the solution repository, Animal.messageOnFeed() is declared to return a FeedResponse object (abstract FeedResponse messageOnFeed()), and a new FeedResponse class is introduced. Subclasses (e.g. Pig, Seal) implement messageOnFeed() to return FeedResponse. This return-type divergence (String vs FeedResponse) creates a real contradiction: students following the problem text will implement messageOnFeed() returning String, while the provided solution and its implementations expect FeedResponse, which will cause compilation/type errors or require non-obvious adaptation and thus will confuse or block students.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return type of Animal.messageOnFeed() consistent across all artifacts. Preferred fix to match the problem text: change the solution to use String returns everywhere (i.e., modify src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java to declare 'public abstract String messageOnFeed();', update all subclasses (Seal, Pig, Goat) to return the required String messages, update Farm methods that print feed messages to accept/print String, and remove the FeedResponse class). Alternatively, if FeedResponse is intentional, update the problem statement and UML to document that messageOnFeed() returns FeedResponse and describe the FeedResponse API and how to extract/print its message. Ensure tests and example usages are updated accordingly.
